analysis: Examined .github/workflows/release-provider.yml (head text lines 1-1068). The visible changes are mostly comments plus the new dev-branch caller (release-dev-branch.yml) calling the same reusable workflow. The comment edits remove the claim that a separate lane self-signs, so every lane signs with $DEVELOPER_ID. Because the dev-branch lane now publishes through the real Developer ID, the trust gate matters: resolve-env checks out `master` (line 136) and runs `provider-release-resume.py verify-source` (line 146) before any credentials are used, with RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT passed in (line 145). The comments say master's gate admits refs/heads/dev for environment dev only, and that resolve-provider-release.sh validates environment against the event and ref (lines 156-160). Neither script is in the supplied evidence, so I could not confirm that a dev push cannot reach staging or prod signing or secrets. Secrets are gated per environment by expressions: PROD_*, STAGING_* and the legacy secrets are empty unless the environment matches (lines 288-299 and 1013-1036). DEV_* secrets are passed unconditionally, which is acceptable. The Apple signing secrets (APPLE_CERTIFICATE_P12, PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64, notarization credentials) are shared across all environments and consumed in build-and-release. Dev-branch content is therefore signed with the production Developer ID. The comments state that source verification gates this, and the code is in scripts not supplied. The signing, notarization and entitlement checks are unchanged in the visible code: get-task-allow absent, aps-environment=production, the self-updater designated requirement, the fan helper requirement, and the CodeDirectory hash recorded. The registration risk for dev builds (T-034, T-054, A-011, A-017) depends on the coordinator and the dev release endpoint, which are out of scope. Remaining questions for integration: (1) release-dev-branch.yml and the verify-source and resolve-provider-release scripts must confirm that the dev-branch lane cannot reach prod or staging, and that the dev branch is protected and reviewed. (2) Dev-signed builds must not be qualified for App Attest serving in prod. No concrete regression is demonstrable from the supplied excerpt.
